<entry id="A02003">
<head-word>אֲמֹורָא</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (אמר) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>speaker, lecturer, interpreter;</italic> esp. 
<italic>Amora</italic>, one who, in lengthy popular discourses, expounds what the lecturer (Tanna, v. 
<xref rid="V00715">תַּנָּא</xref>) says before him in brief and in a low voice; often called מְתוּרְגְּמָן.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 8, end כשם שהדורש … והא' וכ' as the lecturer sits … and the Amora speaks in his presence.—Snh. 7
<sup>b</sup> קום עליה בא' stand by him as an expounder. Taan. 8
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. אוקים … א' עליה ודרש S. … placed an Amora by his side and lectured. Sot. 40
<sup>a</sup> ואמר אֲמֹורֵיה חד טעמא and his Amora gave a different reason. Ḥull. 15
<sup>a</sup> do people listen to the Tanna? לא' צייתי they listen to the Amora.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> in a particular sense אֲמֹורָא, 
<italic>Amora</italic> (
<italic>Amoraïm</italic>), that class of Talmudic authorities who lived after the final redaction of the Mishnah, and whose discussions on the opinions of the 
<italic>Tannaïm</italic> or authors of the 
<italic>Mishnah</italic> and 
<italic>Boraitha</italic>, are deposited in the 
<italic>Guemara</italic>, thus adding a second element to the development of the oral law, called 
<italic>Talmud.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—</italic>
<plural-form>Pl. אֲמֹורִין</plural-form>. Y. Ber. I, 2
<sup>c</sup> top, a. e. תרי א' two Amoraïm differ, for which Babli usually: … אֲמֹורָאֵי נינהו ואליבא two Amoras differ in their relation (or conception) of the opinion of … Shebu. 40
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
